title: A real Qt graphical adapter
lead: Connect TaskModel to real Qt widgets and execute a user scenario inside Nexus.
why: Qt is an additional library, not part of standard C++. It requires its own SDK and build toolchain. In Nexus select Project Studio, create a C++ application and open src/gui.cpp. Building compiles your C++ to Qt/WebAssembly and opens a separate Preview. The lesson’s console Clang/WASI editor contains no Qt and cannot run this exercise.
objectives: Change the success message and rebuild.
Add a count indicator derived from the model.
Test keyboard interaction and empty-input errors.
prerequisites: Modules 1–5: functions, STL, ownership, testing and multi-file builds.
Study the linked prerequisite topics below before this lesson.

concepts.definition: A library of actual graphical application controls.
A Qt notification about an object action or change.
The QObject bounding the lifetime of a callback connection.
A component that automatically arranges widgets.
An isolated execution of the learner’s compiled application.
Item data used here for the domain entity id.
A condition preserved at the boundaries of permitted model operations.
An agreed observation by which a client distinguishes contract satisfaction from a defect.

sections.title: From the model to a real window
paragraphs: Qt is an additional library, not part of standard C++. It requires its own SDK and build toolchain. In Nexus select Project Studio, create a C++ application and open src/gui.cpp. Building compiles your C++ to Qt/WebAssembly and opens a separate Preview. The lesson’s console Clang/WASI editor contains no Qt and cannot run this exercise.

The TaskFlow starter includes a model, CLI, GUI, tests, CMake and target description. Create a new personal project while preserving earlier work. The laboratory changes actual src/gui.cpp; a JavaScript animation or an onClick message in a console does not substitute for execution. Build-service connectivity and source correctness are separate checks.

sections.title: Widgets, layout and ownership
paragraphs: QApplication initializes the graphical environment. TaskWindow derives from QWidget and QVBoxLayout arranges controls vertically without manual coordinates. QLineEdit accepts text, QPushButton represents an action, QListWidget displays tasks and QLabel presents status. Passing this as a parent makes child QObjects owned by the window, so they are not separately deleted when the parent is destroyed.

Do not combine parent ownership with an independent unique_ptr to the same child without analyzing destruction order. The window owns the model by value and the model knows no Qt types. Desktop main uses app.exec; the checked WebAssembly target returns control so the browser can service events. Preserve the supplied conditional branch instead of inserting a busy while loop.

sections.title: Connecting a signal to an action
paragraphs: connect(button, &QPushButton::clicked, this, [this]{add();}) connects a widget signal to a lambda. The third argument is the context and ties connection lifetime to that object. Capturing this permits access to window fields. The arrow accesses a pointed-to object, while &QPushButton::clicked names a class signal rather than invoking it while connecting.

Return in the field and the Add task button call the same add method. It obtains UTF-8, supplies a std::string to model.add, clears the field only on success and refreshes the list. Model exceptions become status feedback rather than escaping the callback. Title rules belong to TaskModel; the GUI handles translation and feedback.

sections.title: Lists, ids and accessibility
paragraphs: Each list item stores t.id in Qt::UserRole. Selection is translated back to a persistent id before complete, so row position does not replace task identity. The list is rebuilt from the model after changes. That is simple for this bounded teaching project; larger data would require measurements and a more incremental view model.

The field receives an accessibleName, long status text wraps and Enter must work without a mouse. Preview checks include focus, understandable labels, empty-input rejection and repetition. An automated basic-input test is not complete VoiceOver or TalkBack acceptance on devices; those checks must be recorded separately and honestly.

sections.title: Changing your own application
paragraphs: First change the window title and successful-add message while preserving model rules. Then add a task-count indicator derived from model.tasks().size() and check it after each accepted action. Do not increment a counter merely because a button was pressed: model rejection creates no task. The changed source must actually be rebuilt.

Retain source, two different builds and an action protocol: an ordinary title, whitespace-only input, repetition, completing a selected item and rejection without selection. The next lesson checks persistence. Complete the work inside Nexus; ZIP supplies an additional portable result, while installing an external IDE is not required to finish the laboratory.

sections.title: Laboratory contract: input to observation
paragraphs: Create a new C++ application in Project Studio. Add a QLabel total-task indicator and derive it from the model during refresh. Preserve Add/Enter/Complete/Save, the Task title accessible name and NXTF1. Empty or whitespace-only titles must not create tasks.

Trace the first reference scenario before running. Enter learn C++ and press Enter. One open task; the count reflects the model. Relate each algorithm step to state changes, distinguishing rejection from the point where a change is committed.

sections.title: Reading a working example
paragraphs: The window creates an input, list and buttons. Return invokes C++ add and the model validates text. refresh displays actual tasks and emits NEXUS_TASKS. First identify data, ownership and the observable outcome. Then change exactly one initial condition and predict which observation changes. This connects syntax to a contract rather than memorizing finished source text.

The second version adds a count QLabel. refresh reads model size rather than button-press count. Empty-input rejection does not increase the count. Compare the second example with the first: what new boundary is covered, and which test distinguishes the correct implementation from a superficially similar mistake? Retain both sources, predictions and actual observations so that the explanation can be reproduced.

sections.title: Independent checking and transfer
paragraphs: Test keyboard interaction and empty-input errors. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Begin with a specification and input bounds; the worked function is a scaffold, not the requirements of another domain. State an independent expectation before execution so that a test is not fitted to accidental output.

Design a completed-task filter without changing ids. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Record decisions, a rejected alternative, checked scenarios and remaining limitations. Independently complete the final assessment control-change task and explain which files, tests and observations it affects. An additional peer or teacher requirement is optional review.

files.CMakeLists.txt:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(TaskFlow LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
add_library(task_model src/task_model.cpp)
target_include_directories(task_model PUBLIC include)
if(EMSCRIPTEN)
 target_compile_options(task_model PUBLIC -fexceptions)
 target_link_options(task_model INTERFACE -fexceptions)
endif()
add_executable(taskflow_cli src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(taskflow_cli PRIVATE task_model)
enable_testing()
add_executable(taskflow_tests tests/task_model_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(taskflow_tests PRIVATE task_model)
add_test(NAME task_model COMMAND taskflow_tests)
option(NEXUS_GUI "Build the Qt GUI" OFF)
if(EMSCRIPTEN)
 set(NEXUS_GUI ON)
endif()
if(NEXUS_GUI)
 find_package(Qt6 6.8 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Widgets)
 qt_add_executable(program MANUAL_FINALIZATION src/gui.cpp)
 target_link_libraries(program PRIVATE task_model Qt6::Widgets)
 if(EMSCRIPTEN)
  target_compile_options(program PRIVATE -fexceptions)
  target_link_options(program PRIVATE -fexceptions -sDISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=0 -sDYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 "-sEXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=['FS']" -sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1)
 endif()
 qt_finalize_executable(program)
endif()

actions: Enter learn C++ and press Enter.
cases.expected: One open task; the count reflects the model.

actions: Leave the input empty and activate Add task.
cases.expected: A validation error; task count is unchanged.

actions: Enter three spaces and press Enter.
cases.expected: Rejection; input remains available for correction.

actions: Activate Complete selected with an empty list.
cases.expected: Select a task feedback; the model is unchanged.
Two tasks with distinct ids: duplicate titles are permitted.

actions: Add a task; save application data, save through the panel, Stop and Run.
cases.expected: The task is restored from taskflow.txt and sources are preserved.

actions: Add two tasks, select the second and complete it.
cases.expected: Only the second task is completed; repetition does not increase done.

actions: Stop Preview, change a C++ label and rebuild.
cases.expected: New build text appears; an earlier submitted revision stays unchanged.

assessment.question: A user enters only spaces and activates Add. What behaviour is specified?
answers: Input is cleared and rejection counts as a successful addition.
No task is created and rejected input remains for correction.
A task with an empty title is created.
assessment.explanation: The model validates title and the adapter clears input only on success. This distinguishes rejection from acceptance.

assessment.question: Why should a total QLabel derive its value from tasks().size() during refresh?
answers: To require changing NXTF1.
To reflect the model after loading and any commands rather than only Add clicks.
To retain a separate independent click counter.
assessment.explanation: A derived view is recomputed from its source of truth. A separate click counter can diverge from a loaded model.

assessment.question: A QLabel is created with parent this. What is dangerous to add without ownership analysis?
answers: Calling setText while the window is alive.
An independent owner that may outlive deletion of the child by its Qt parent.
A non-owning pointer used to update text.
assessment.explanation: The Qt parent manages child lifetime. A second independent deletion path requires coordination; an observing pointer does not itself release the resource.

assessment.question: Message source was edited but Preview was not rebuilt. What does the old window establish?
answers: Behaviour of the new version because its file was saved.
That the compiler automatically rewrote the old Wasm.
Only behaviour of the previously built version.
assessment.explanation: A build belongs to a source snapshot. Edited text requires rebuilding and repeating the observed scenario.

assessment.question: After filtering, the first visible row belongs to id 2. How should complete identify its target?
answers: Using the id stored in UserRole.
Always using row+1.
Using the total visible-row count.
assessment.explanation: Filtering changes position rather than task identity. UserRole connects the row to its persistent model id.

readinessCheck.question: Why should model.cpp not include QApplication merely for a GUI adapter?
answers: Otherwise tasks cannot be stored in a vector.
C++ prohibits separate model and GUI files.
It would add a GUI dependency to the model and its independent tests.
readinessCheck.explanation: Separating model and adapter preserves CLI/tests builds without Qt. The GUI dependency belongs to the GUI target.

readinessCheck.question: What does a callback retaining non-owning receiver access require?
answers: A lifetime guarantee or checked weak access before invocation.
Replacing the raw address with a const pointer is sufficient.
A std::function copy automatically extends every captured reference lifetime.
readinessCheck.explanation: A callback name does not manage lifetime. Receiver closure is a separate scenario requiring design and tests.

readinessCheck.question: Can the domain rule complete be tested without a real GUI?
answers: Yes, but only replace the model with an unrelated JS mock-up.
Yes, invoke the same model from a separate driver.
No, the rule must run only inside paint.
readinessCheck.explanation: The driver checks the actual C++ model. It does not establish GUI accessibility, but GUI is not needed for domain logic.

reflection: Which check distinguishes a superficially similar incorrect implementation?
Design a completed-task filter without changing ids.

endif()

sections.title: Connecting a signal to an action
paragraphs: connect(button, &QPushButton::clicked, this, [this]{add();}) connects a widget signal to a lambda. The third argument is the context and ties connection lifetime to that object. Capturing this permits access to window fields. The arrow accesses a pointed-to object, while &QPushButton::clicked names a class signal rather than invoking it while connecting.

Return in the field and the Add task button call the same add method. It obtains UTF-8, supplies a std::string to model.add, clears the field only on success and refreshes the list. Model exceptions become status feedback rather than escaping the callback. Title rules belong to TaskModel; the GUI handles translation and feedback.

sections.title: Lists, ids and accessibility
paragraphs: Each list item stores t.id in Qt::UserRole. Selection is translated back to a persistent id before complete, so row position does not replace task identity. The list is rebuilt from the model after changes. That is simple for this bounded teaching project; larger data would require measurements and a more incremental view model.

The field receives an accessibleName, long status text wraps and Enter must work without a mouse. Preview checks include focus, understandable labels, empty-input rejection and repetition. An automated basic-input test is not complete VoiceOver or TalkBack acceptance on devices; those checks must be recorded separately and honestly.

sections.title: From a base window to your own counter
paragraphs: Compare the extended src/gui.cpp with the base. The extended example uses count_ to show the total Tasks count. Your task observes something different: Open tasks counts only tasks with done=false, so completion decreases it without deleting a task.

sections.title: Changing your own application
paragraphs: First change the window title and successful-add message while preserving model rules. Then add a task-count indicator derived from model.tasks().size() and check it after each accepted action. Do not increment a counter merely because a button was pressed: model rejection creates no task. The changed source must actually be rebuilt.

Retain source, two different builds and an action protocol: an ordinary title, whitespace-only input, repetition, completing a selected item and rejection without selection. The next lesson checks persistence. Complete the work inside Nexus; ZIP supplies an additional portable result, while installing an external IDE is not required to finish the laboratory.

sections.title: Laboratory contract: input to observation
paragraphs: Create a new C++ application in Project Studio. Add a QLabel total-task indicator and derive it from the model during refresh. Preserve Add/Enter/Complete/Save, the Task title accessible name and NXTF1. Empty or whitespace-only titles must not create tasks.

Trace the first reference scenario before running. Enter learn C++ and press Enter. One open task; the count reflects the model. Relate each algorithm step to state changes, distinguishing rejection from the point where a change is committed.

sections.title: Reading a working example
paragraphs: The window creates an input, list and buttons. Return invokes C++ add and the model validates text. refresh displays actual tasks and emits NEXUS_TASKS. First identify data, ownership and the observable outcome. Then change exactly one initial condition and predict which observation changes. This connects syntax to a contract rather than memorizing finished source text.

The second version adds a count QLabel. refresh reads model size rather than button-press count. Empty-input rejection does not increase the count. Compare the second example with the first: what new boundary is covered, and which test distinguishes the correct implementation from a superficially similar mistake? Retain both sources, predictions and actual observations so that the explanation can be reproduced.

sections.title: Independent checking and transfer
paragraphs: Test keyboard interaction and empty-input errors. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Begin with a specification and input bounds; the worked function is a scaffold, not the requirements of another domain. State an independent expectation before execution so that a test is not fitted to accidental output.

Design a completed-task filter without changing ids. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Record decisions, a rejected alternative, checked scenarios and remaining limitations. Independently complete the final assessment control-change task and explain which files, tests and observations it affects. An additional peer or teacher requirement is optional review.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Create a separate copy of the complete file bundle. Add an Open tasks QLabel and count only unfinished model tasks in refresh. Change the success text, rebuild the actual C++ and check the keyboard scenario.
Open all project files and locate entry src/gui.cpp.

selfcheck.prompt: Which visible state remains after accepting alpha, then entering three spaces and pressing Return?
selfcheck.feedback: Visible observation: one list row after alpha; after spaces, the same row and an editable input. NEXUS_TASKS is diagnostic telemetry; it does not replace inspecting the window.

In Nexus use Project Studio to edit, build, run, test and submit.
Optional native model/CLI build: cmake -S . -B build -DNEXUS_GUI=OFF; cmake --build build; ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure.

options: One task; spaces remain in the field; an error is shown.

selfcheck.prompt: A user enters only spaces and activates Add. What behaviour is specified?
options: Input is cleared and rejection counts as a successful addition.
No task is created and rejected input remains for correction.
A task with an empty title is created.
selfcheck.feedback: The model validates title and the adapter clears input only on success. This distinguishes rejection from acceptance.

selfcheck.prompt: Why should a total QLabel derive its value from tasks().size() during refresh?
options: To reflect the model after loading and any commands rather than only Add clicks.
To retain a separate independent click counter.
selfcheck.feedback: A derived view is recomputed from its source of truth. A separate click counter can diverge from a loaded model.

selfcheck.prompt: A QLabel is created with parent this. What is dangerous to add without ownership analysis?
options: Calling setText while the window is alive.
An independent owner that may outlive deletion of the child by its Qt parent.
A non-owning pointer used to update text.
selfcheck.feedback: The Qt parent manages child lifetime. A second independent deletion path requires coordination; an observing pointer does not itself release the resource.

selfcheck.prompt: Message source was edited but Preview was not rebuilt. What does the old window establish?
options: Behaviour of the new version because its file was saved.
That the compiler automatically rewrote the old Wasm.
Only behaviour of the previously built version.
selfcheck.feedback: A build belongs to a source snapshot. Edited text requires rebuilding and repeating the observed scenario.

selfcheck.prompt: After filtering, the first visible row belongs to id 2. How should complete identify its target?
options: Using the id stored in UserRole.
selfcheck.feedback: Filtering changes position rather than task identity. UserRole connects the row to its persistent model id.

selfcheck.prompt: Why update total from model.tasks().size() instead of incrementing it for each press? How does connect’s context relate to the window lifetime?
selfcheck.feedback: Rejection creates no task; repeated complete creates none either. The model is the source of truth. Context this ties the connection to a live window; child QObjects belong to the window through parent.

practice.title: Laboratory: A real Qt graphical adapter
practice.task: In a separate base TaskFlow copy, add an Open tasks: N QLabel that counts only tasks with done=false in refresh. The example shows total Tasks; here completion must reduce Open tasks without deleting the task. Change the successful-add message. Preserve Add/Return, Complete selected, accessible name Task title and NXTF1. Run all listed scenarios, including repeated complete and Stop/Run after explicit saving.

# TaskFlow — portable C++20 project

In Nexus use Project Studio to edit, build, run, test and submit.
Optional native model/CLI build: cmake -S . -B build -DNEXUS_GUI=OFF; cmake --build build; ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure.
GUI: Qt 6.8.3; WebAssembly: Emscripten 3.1.56.
Data: taskflow.txt / NXTF1. Preserve old projects and never include credentials.

cases.label: Ordinary addition
cases.input: Enter learn C++ and press Enter.
cases.output: One open task; the count reflects the model.

cases.label: Empty title
cases.input: Leave the input empty and activate Add task.
cases.output: A validation error; task count is unchanged.

cases.label: Whitespace title
cases.input: Enter three spaces and press Enter.
cases.output: Rejection; input remains available for correction.

cases.label: Complete without selection
cases.input: Activate Complete selected with an empty list.
cases.output: Select a task feedback; the model is unchanged.

cases.label: Repeated title
cases.output: Two tasks with distinct ids: duplicate titles are permitted.

cases.label: Explicit persistence
cases.input: Add a task; save application data, save through the panel, Stop and Run.
cases.output: The task is restored from taskflow.txt and sources are preserved.

cases.label: Selecting a persistent id
cases.input: Add two tasks, select the second and complete it.
cases.output: Only the second task is completed; repetition does not increase done.

cases.label: Stop and continue
cases.input: Stop Preview, change a C++ label and rebuild.
cases.output: New build text appears; an earlier submitted revision stays unchanged.

cases.label: Your task: open count instead of total
cases.input: Add alpha and beta. Complete alpha, repeat its completion, then complete beta.
cases.output: Open tasks: 2 → 1 → 1 → 0. Both tasks remain in the model.

criteria: The base window contains Task title, Add task, Complete selected and Save application data.
Before adding: open 0; after alpha: open 1; after completing it: open 0, with the task retained in the model.
alpha is restored; the new success message appears after an actual rebuild.
Add one valid scenario and one rejection of your own. Keep the sources, input/actions and observed outcome. Your explanation is reviewed separately from execution.
practice.hint: Rejection creates no task; repeated complete creates none either. The model is the source of truth. Context this ties the connection to a live window; child QObjects belong to the window through parent.

steps.action: Open all project files and locate entry src/gui.cpp.
steps.why: Qt requires its own headers, library and build.
steps.expected: The base window contains Task title, Add task, Complete selected and Save application data.

steps.action: Add an Open tasks QLabel and count !task.done in refresh.
steps.why: One update point keeps the counter consistent with every accepted change.
steps.expected: Before adding: open 0; after alpha: open 1; after completing it: open 0, with the task retained in the model.

steps.action: Run the listed scenarios, explicitly save data, then Stop/Run.
steps.why: Running-window data and a saved file have different lifetimes.
steps.expected: alpha is restored; the new success message appears after an actual rebuild.

starterObservation.description: The base window accepts alpha and displays one task. The indicator required by your task is still absent; complete the TODO and rebuild the project.
